overview: This 617-page file traces U.S. and Japanese efforts to stabilize Japan’s postwar economy in 1948–49. Directives, reports, policy studies, and correspondence examine the Dodge program, budgets, prices, exchange rates, exports, and prospects for self-support. They also record disputes over deconcentration and the gradual reduction of Occupation economic controls.
interest: Japanese policy studies and U.S. correspondence reveal competing views of austerity, recovery, self-support, and Occupation control.
